summary: All 23 SRanger requirements are implemented in 9 Java files (one controller, three modes, six step() transitions plus the initial mode). No requirement is unimplemented. Three invented defaults, five design choices and one model-fidelity question are listed for review.

issues.title: Sensor no-reading value is 1000.0 m
issues.raw: SR-DM5 asks for 'a large default value' when no IR reading is available but gives no number.
issues.fix_directive: None needed unless the specification fixes a value; 1000.0 m is far above OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD, so missing data can never satisfy obstacleDetected.

issues.title: Negative or NaN readings are treated as 'no reading'
issues.raw: SR-DM5 / SR-SF1 say distance() is non-negative but do not say what to do with an invalid measurement.
issues.fix_directive: None needed; Sensor.update stores the no-reading default for any reading that is not >= 0.0, so distance() is always non-negative.

issues.title: Initial values of clockResetTime and of the actuator's last command
issues.raw: SR-Var1 does not give clockResetTime a value before Turning is first entered; SR-DM6 does not say what the actuator holds before the first command.
issues.fix_directive: None needed; both start at 0.0. clockResetTime is only read in Turning, which always sets it first; the actuator's 0.0/0.0 is overwritten by the constructor's initial Move.

issues.title: Moving -> Turning needs both the obstacle event and obstacleDetected
issues.raw: SR-Beh2 triggers the transition on the obstacle event; SR-GP1 says obstacleDetected (distance <= obstacleThreshold) is the guard on the same transition.
issues.fix_directive: Implemented as trigger obstacle with condition obstacleDetected. On this branch clockResetTime is reset before Move(0, turnVel) is issued, the order SR-Beh2 states.

issues.title: Priority in Turning: endTask, then the timed exit, then tick
issues.raw: The requirements give no priority between SR-Beh5 (autonomous, timed), SR-Beh6 (endTask) and SR-Beh7 (tick). tick arrives every cycle, so if tick came first the timed exit could never fire.
issues.fix_directive: endTask is first in both Moving and Turning (it is the shutdown). The timed exit comes before tick, and the tick self-loop conjoins !turnDurationElapsed so the two are exclusive in the model.

issues.title: Initial Move(moveVel, 0) is issued in the constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1 and SR-Beh1: Moving is initial and entering Moving issues Move(moveVel, 0). There is no transition into the initial mode in step().
issues.fix_directive: The constructor issues the initial Move after wiring sensor, actuator and clock. If the extractor does not model constructor actions, Moving's entry action still comes from the Turning -> Moving branch.

issues.title: tick self-loops perform no action
issues.raw: SR-Beh4 and SR-Beh7 say the controller performs no action on the tick self-loop; the general rule is that a branch performs the target mode's entry actions.
issues.fix_directive: The requirement wins: the tick branches only re-assign the mode and do not re-issue Move or reset the clock.

issues.title: Clock is monotonic seconds since construction, held in a field named timer
issues.raw: SR-Var1 needs 'the current time' but no time source is specified; 'clock' is a RoboChart reserved word.
issues.fix_directive: None needed; Clock.now() returns System.nanoTime() seconds since the Clock was created, and the controller field holding it is named timer.

issues.title: OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD = 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model
issues.raw: The model's constants interface rounds a fractional constant up to the next integer, and obstacleDetected compares against OBSTACLE_THRESHOLD; the other three constants are whole numbers.
issues.fix_directive: The Java keeps 0.5 as SR-DM2 requires. In the model the guard reads distance <= 1, so verified properties that depend on the exact threshold describe a slightly larger detection zone.

next_step: Run the pipeline (compile, coverage, profile check, transformations, FDR4, Dafny, Isabelle, vacuity) and fix the Java from the failing phases' reports.
